text:
maria: Heads up — after the Cilium 1.20.0 rollout to west2-gpu, we're seeing pod-to-pod packet loss and huge east-west latency for GPU training jobs. lots of retransmits.
ryan: :eyes: noticed similar on a few GPU nodes, GPU pods timing out while syncing checkpoints. Any common kernel/sysctl changes from the upgrade?
devops-bot: deploy finished: cilium-daemonset v1.20.0 -> rolled to nodes west2-gpu-{a,b,c} at 2025-11-14T09:12:01Z
jia: quick repro: run iperf pod->pod across same node and across nodes. intra-node is OK, cross-node shows 15–30% packet loss and MTU errors in dmesg.
maria: pasted logs: ```
# ip r show
10.0.0.0/16 dev cilium_host proto kernel scope link src 10.0.3.5
# dmesg | tail -n 5
[ 12345.678901] cilium: dropped 1424 frag needed and DF set
[ 12345.679002] net_ratelimit: 5 callbacks suppressed
```
kevin: that frag message screams MTU mismatch / tunneling change. Did the Cilium change encapsulation defaults?
ryan: previously we were on Geneve with mtu 9000 on the nodes (eni jumbo). The new agent seems to flip to vxlan or set tunnel mtu to 1450 when it detects cloud overlay. Not sure why it switched for west2-gpu only.
maria: confirmed agent config on one node: `--tunnel=auto` and `--mtu-overwrite=1450` present in the new daemonset. I didn't see that in 1.19 manifest.
jia: run `kubectl exec` tcpdump on host veth: shows lots of ICMP frag-needed from intermediate when pkt > 1500. Also RDMA jobs report 'connect delay' on NCCL.
ryan: RDMA is fragile with fragmentation. If tunnel MTU/DF interaction changed, that'll break GPUDirect across nodes.
kevin: can we hotfix: set cilium configmap to force tunnel=disabled and host-mtu=9000? Or revert to 1.19 until we figure root cause.
maria: tried configmap patch -> cilium pods restart but nodes still showed 1450 in cilium-agent logs (config override not picked up). I think the operator reconciled and used the new default.
sre-oncall: I'm going to pause further rollouts to remaining regions and open an incident. tagging infra lead.
ryan: workaround I pushed to a couple problematic nodes: `ip link set dev cilium_host mtu 9000` and restart kube-proxy on node — reduced packet loss to <2% for cross-node. Not ideal but buys time.
maria: thanks. Can we safe-ship that as a script? Also need to ensure kube-proxy iptables rules not rewriting DF flags.
jia: I'll run a quick canary with 3 GPU jobs pinned to patched nodes for a couple hours and monitor retransmits + NCCL barrier times.
kevin: filing upstream bug with Cilium — likely regression in tunnel auto-detection when ENI reports jumbo supported. Include `kubectl get pods -n kube-system cilium -o yaml`, `cilium-agent` logs and `ip link` dumps.
maria: +1. Also capture `ethtool -k` and `sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh` outputs.
devops-bot: incident created: INC-20251114-02 "cilium tunnel MTU regression affecting east-west on west2-gpu" assigned to eng-infra oncall.
sre-oncall: assigning to @ryan and @maria. Please paste mitigation steps in the incident doc.
ryan: mitigation steps I ran: 1) cordon nodes not to schedule new GPU jobs 2) run `ip link set cilium_host mtu 9000` 3) restart cilium-agent pod on node 4) validate with iperf -> <2% loss 5) revert rollout to 1.19 via daemonset image tag (blocked because operator resets)
maria: final note — we should bake an explicit `--tunnel=geneve` and `--host-mtu=9000` into our cilium manifests for GPU pools until they fix auto mode. I'll open a PR and link to the incident. :thumbsup:
